rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says tasbīḥ with praise may mean uttering the formula ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God,’ or declaring God free of evil and extolling Him in meaning.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن قوله تعالى : ( وسبح بحمد ربك ) أمر بالتسبيح مقرونا بالحمد

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: The literal reading is the formula ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God’; the semantic reading declares God transcendent and extols Him.
rows.anchor: إما أن يراد اللفظ أي قل سبحان الله والحمد لله أو يراد المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: A report cited by Ibn ʿAṭiyya says whoever glorifies God seventy times at sunset has his sins depart with the setting sun.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر ذكره ابن عطية من سبح عند غروب الشمس سبعين تسبيحة غربت بذنوبه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim allows tasbīḥ to mean declaring God transcendent and majestic, occupying oneself with this at the named times.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : لا يبعد حمل ذلك على التنزيه والاجلال والمعنى اشتغل بتنزيه الله

rows.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām likewise reads tasbīḥ as transcendence and takes the bāʾ in ‘with praise’ instrumentally.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك حمله أيضا العز بن عبد السلام وجعل الباء في قوله سبحانه : ( بحمد ربك )

rows.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: For al-ʿIzz, negating deficiencies affirms their opposites, attributes of perfection; praise may be annexed to its agent, object, or by specification.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك لتعيين سلب صفات النقص لأن من سلب شيئا فقد اثبت ضده واضداد صفات النقص صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors annexing the verbal noun praise to its agent, since complete true praise is God’s praise of Himself.
rows.anchor: ثم استحسن الأول لأن الحمد الحق الكامل حمد الله تعالى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent parsing takes the bāʾ as accompaniment and praise as a verbal noun whose object is God.
rows.anchor: والمتبادر جعل الباء للملابسة والإضافة من إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam prefers tasbīḥ as declaring God free of shirk, closest to context because the Prophet is told to endure denial and association of partners.
rows.anchor: واختار الإمام حمل التسبيح على التنزيه من الشرك وقال : أنه اقرب إلى الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says this reading does not explain the specified times; an answer treats them as signs of continual glorification, as at dawn and evening.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأنه لا وجه حينئذ لتخصيص هذه الأوقات بالذكر وايجيب بأن المراد بذكرها الدلالة على الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author responds that ‘some of the night’ resists a merely continuous reading; the first command may be general and the second particularized for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ورد بأنه يأباه من التبعيضية في قوله سبحانه ( من إناء الليل ) على أن هذه الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes tasbīḥ in its apparent sense and praise as prayer, with the time phrase attached to prayer to explain its specification.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يكون المراد بالتسبيح ما هو الظاهر منه ويكون المراد من الحمد الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer fits the command to endure and recalls seeking help through patience and prayer; reports support prayer here.
rows.anchor: بأن الأنسب بالأمر بالصبر الأمر بالصلاة ليكون ذلك ارشادا لما تضمنه قوله تعالى : ( واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaraf can mean a portion or group of something, as recorded in al-Ṣiḥāḥ and al-Qāmūs.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد بالطرف طائفة من الشئ فانه أحد معانيه كما في الصحاح والقاموس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ‘so that you may be pleased’ modifies glorification, it promises a pleasing reward and is evidence God is under no obligation to reward anyone.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو متعلق بسبح أي سبح في هذه الأوقات رجاء أن تنال عنده تعالى ماترضى به نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may modify patience and prayer, with satisfaction meaning worldly victory and the mission’s spread.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون متعلقا بالأمر بالصبر والأمر بالصلاة والمراد ( لعلك ترضى ) في الدنيا بحصول الظفر

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وأبو بكر وأبان وعصمة وأبو عمارة عن حفص وأبو زيد عن المفضل وأبو عبيد ومحمد بن عيسى الأصفهاني
rows.claim: These reciters read tarḍā in the passive, meaning ‘your Lord will make you pleased.’
rows.anchor: وقرا أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وابو بكر وابان وعصمة وابو عمارة عن حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping God ‘on an edge’ depicts an unstable person at a military line’s edge, staying if victory seems likely and fleeing otherwise.
rows.anchor: على طرف من الدين لا ثبات له فيه كالذي يكون في طرف الجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good fortune that reassures this wavering worshipper is worldly prosperity, health, or children, not believers’ steadfast reassurance.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الخير الخير الدنيوي كالرخاء والعافية والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affliction can harm the person, family, or property; turning on one’s face means rushing ahead or fleeing, and al-Kashf calls it defeat by metonymy.
rows.anchor: أي شيء يفتن به من مكروه يعتريه في نفسه أو أهله أو ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes turning on the face as anxiety, since it contrasts with reassurance; the person reverts from religion to unbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ههنا عبارة عن القلق لأنه في مقابلة اطمأن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a newcomer to Medina judged the religion good if his wife bore a son and his horses produced foals, but bad otherwise.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردوية عن ابن عباس أنه قال في هذه الآية : كان الرجل يقدم المدينة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that a Jewish convert who lost sight, wealth, and children asked the Prophet to release him; the Prophet refused and compared Islam’s refining effect to fire purifying metal. Ibn Ḥajar weakened it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردوية عن أبي سعيد قال : أسلم رجل من اليهود فذهب بصره وماله وولده فتشاءم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: The verse is also said to concern Shayba ibn Rabīʿa, who accepted Islam before the Prophet’s public emergence and later apostatized.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في شيبة ابن ربيعة أسلم قبل ظهوره عليه الصلاة والسلام وارتد بعد ظهوره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also reports that the verse was revealed concerning hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنها نزلت في المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He loses this world and the next’ may stand independently, be apposition to ‘turned back’ per al-Rāzī, or be circumstantial per Abū Ḥayyān; it means forfeiting both worlds.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة أو بدل من انقلب كما قال أبو الفضل الرازي

rows.speaker: مجاهد وحميد والأعرج وابن محيصن وقنب والجحدري وابن مقسم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce khāsiran accusative as a circumstantial accusative; the nominative makes it subject of inqalaba and replaces the pronoun with an explicit noun to explain the reversal by loss.
rows.anchor: خاسر بزنة فاعل منصوبا على الحال لأن إضافته لفظية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative khāsir may be a predicate of an omitted subject, expressing blame; a reading as tajrīd is also proposed for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقريء خاسر بالرفع على أنه فاعل انقلب وفيه وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the loss; its distance signals extremity, though another explanation is that the referent is not explicitly named.
rows.anchor: في غاية ما يكون وقيل إن أداة البعد لكونه المشار إليه غير مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī glosses al-khusrān al-mubīn as unmistakable loss, with no other possible description.
rows.anchor: أي الواضح كونه خسرانا لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ḥattā begins a sentence and marks the endpoint of an omitted prior clause; the ‘even Kalīb insults me’ example leaves the statement that everyone insults the speaker implicit.
rows.anchor: ابتدائية وغاية لمقدر يدل عليه ما قبلها والتقدير فلا أكون كالكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it attaches to the second ‘they describe,’ making slander last until death; ‘say, Lord’ interrupts to urge protection from Satan and obedience to repel evil graciously.
rows.anchor: حتى متعلقة بمحذوف يدل عليه كأنه قيل : لا يزالون على سوء المقالة والطعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching ḥattā to the first ‘they describe’ or to ‘they associate partners’ is judged untenable.
rows.anchor: على ( يصفون ) الأول أو على ( يشركون ) وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links the passage to ‘they are liars’: denying God a son through this point interrupts the discourse to establish their lies and deserved punishment; al-Ālūsī rejects it.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن يكون مرورا على قوله تعالى ( وإنهم لكاذبون )

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows ḥattā to begin a sentence without endpoint force; Abū Ḥayyān objects that it necessarily retains endpoint meaning.
rows.anchor: من كلام ابن عطية أنه يجوز أن تكون ( حتى ) هنا ابتدائية لا غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘one of them’ refers to unbelievers; death’s arrival means signs of death and conditions of the next life appear.
rows.anchor: أن ضمير ( أحدهم ) راجع إلى الكفار والمراد من مجيء الموت ظهور أماراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural imperative ‘return me’ may honor God, as poetry shows one person addressed in plural; the author rejects denial of this usage.
rows.anchor: والواو لتعظيم المخاطب وهو الله تعالى كما في قوله : ألا فاحموني يا إله محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plural addresses angels, with ‘my Lord’s angels’ understood, or ‘Lord’ invokes God while ‘return me’ addresses angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الواو لكون الخطاب للملائكة عليهم السلام والكلام على تقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: ابن جرير عن ابن جريج
rows.claim: A report relayed by Ibn Jurayj says believers offered return reject it as return to grief, whereas unbelievers ask God to send them back.
rows.anchor: أخرجه ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن ابن جرير قال : زعموا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المازني
rows.claim: Al-Māzinī says the plural pronoun signals repeated pleading, so ‘return me’ means it three times; he compares the dual in qifā nabki.
rows.anchor: جمع الضمير ليدل على التكرار فكأنه قال : رب أرجعني أرجعني أرجعني

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī objects that the singular imperative’s underlying form contains no plural pronoun, leaving al-Māzinī’s metaphor unexplained.
rows.anchor: واستشكل ذلك الخفاجي بأنه كان أصل ارجعوا مثلا ارجع ارجع ارجع لم يكن ضمير الجمع

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī proposes substituting one word-form for another without regard to meaning, letting the plural pronoun signal repetition for emphasis.
rows.anchor: استعارة لفظ مكان لفظ آخر لنكتة بقطع النظر عن معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Khafājī went too far: plural is an honorific address to one treated as a group, making the action resemble repeated group action.
rows.anchor: أراد المازني أنه جمع الضمير للتعظيم بتنزيل المخاطب الواحد منزلة الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanation extends to the dual in qifā nabki only if dual address can honor one person; al-Ālūsī does not recall seeing this and leaves it open.
rows.anchor: لكن إجراء نحو هذا في نحو قفا نبك لا يتسنى إلا إذا قيل بأنه قد يقصد بضمير التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In what I left behind’ may mean abandoned faith; laʿalla may express hope about both work and faith despite knowing return will not happen, or only work because faith on return is certain.
rows.anchor: أي في الإيمان الذي تركته ولعل للترجي وهو إما راجع للعمل والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, what was left is wealth or worldly life; laʿalla may also express purpose.
rows.anchor: فيما تركت من المال أو من الدنيا جعل مفارقة ذلك تركا له ويجوز أن تكون لعل للتعليل

rows.speaker: البغوي عن الواقدي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī cites al-Wāqidī that every Qur’anic laʿalla signals purpose except ‘perhaps you will live forever’ (26:129); al-Suddī’s route from Abū Mālik says similarly.
rows.anchor: حكى البغوي عن الواقدي أن جميع ما في القرآن من لعل فإنها للتعليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The wish to return is not confined to unbelievers: Ibn ʿAbbās says one who withheld zakāt or could afford pilgrimage but did not do it asks to return at death.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن مانع الزكاة وتارك الحج المستطيع يسألان الرجعة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report through al-Daylamī from Jābir says at death things obstructing truth appear before a person’s eyes, prompting the plea to return; this supports reading what was left as wealth.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عن جابر بن عبد الله قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حضر الإنسان الوفاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes and dismisses the request to return as impossible.
rows.anchor: ردع عن طلب الرجعة واستبعاد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘It is a word he says’ means the dying person inevitably utters it in regret; fronting the subject gives emphasis or exclusivity.
rows.anchor: لا محالة لا يخليها ولا يسكت عنها لاستيلاء الحسرة وتسلط الندم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lone-word phrase depicts futile speech receiving no answer, like the retort to occupy oneself alone with pointless speech; kalimah means speech.
rows.anchor: اشتغل أنت وحدك بهذه الكلمة فتكلم واستمع يعني أنها مما لا تسمع منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians treat kalimah meaning ‘speech’ as figurative, while lexicographers consider it literal or familiar metaphor.
rows.anchor: الكلمة هنا بمعنى الكلام كما في قولهم : كلمة الشهادة وهي في هذا المعنى مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the dying person says kallā to himself; kallā and what follows are God’s speech.
rows.anchor: وما بعدها من كلامه تعالى وأبعد جدا من زعم أن ( كلا ) من قول من عاين الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾahum means ‘before them’; the pronoun refers to one dying person in wording but to all in meaning.
rows.anchor: أي أمامهم وقد مر تحقيقه والضمير لأحدهم والجمع باعتبار المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh is a barrier between the dead and return, lasting until they are raised.
rows.anchor: حاجز بينهم وبين الرجعة ( إلى يوم يبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barzakh lasts from the graves until resurrection, making worldly return impossible like a camel passing through a needle’s eye.
rows.anchor: من قبورهم وهو يوم القيامة وهذا تعليق لرجعتهم إلى الدنيا بالمحال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd defines the barzakh as a barrier between death and resurrection, spanning the wait before people rise from graves.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أن المراد من ورائهم حاجز بين الموت والبعث في القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view makes the barzakh a barrier to complete requital that remains until Judgment Day, when full recompense comes.
rows.anchor: حاجز بينهم وبين الجزاء التام باق إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is blown for Resurrection in the second blast, when resurrection and gathering occur.
rows.anchor: وهي النفخة الثانية التي يقع عندها البعث والنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively ṣūr means plural ṣūrah, image: souls are blown into bodies. Readings from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿIyāḍ, and Ibn Razīn support this; it can coincide with blowing the horn.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى فإذا نفخ في الأجساد أرواحها على أن الصور جمع صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship will not benefit people: terror and absorption in each person’s fate make family ties effectively nonexistent, as the cited flight from relatives illustrates.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنها لا تنفعهم شيئا فهي منزلة منزلة العدم لعظم الهول

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports a public call on Judgment Day inviting anyone owed a right or grievance to claim it, even when the debtor is family; this supports a general reading.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المبارك في الزهد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from Maswar ibn Makhrama and Ibn ʿUmar preserve the Prophetic exception that every bond and lineage is severed except his; al-Ālūsī accepts it but limits benefit to related believers.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرج جماعة نحوه عن مسور بن مخرمة رضي الله تعالى عنه مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lineage report does not limit the verse: just after the second blast people do not notice or think of kinship, describing terror rather than denying benefit to believers.
rows.anchor: نعم ينبغي القول بأن نفع نسبه صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما هو بالنسبة للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجبائي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Jubbāʾī say people will not boast of lineage but pride themselves on deeds and escape from terrors; on this reading negation is figurative.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وحكى عن الجبائي أن المراد أنه لا يفتخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding ‘beneficial,’ ‘noticed,’ or ‘boasted of’ to ‘lineages’ is possible but weak; the time adverb attaches to ‘among them,’ not ‘lineages.’
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون فيه صفة مقدرة أي فلا أنساب نافعة أو ملتفتا إليها أو مفتخرا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not ask about identity or condition because each is absorbed in himself; silence begins just after the second blast, before or after recognition.
rows.anchor: ولا يسأل بعضهم بعضا عن حاله وممن هو ونحو ذلك لاشتغال كل منهم بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later mutual questioning may occur near Hell for unbelievers and in Paradise for believers; the negation may mean recognition or requests for benefit, unlike later blame or companionship.
rows.anchor: ولعله عند جهنم وهو بعد النفخة الثانية بكثير وكذا تساؤل المؤمنين بعدها بكثير أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One Ibn ʿAbbās report puts absent questioning at the first blast and its return at the second; his other report takes this verse’s blast as the second and allows other reconciliations.
rows.anchor: وروي جماعة عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه سئل عن وجه الجمع بين النفي هنا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the verb with a doubled sīn, yusāʾalūn, ‘they are questioned.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( ولا يساءلون ) بتشديد السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales may mean measured good deeds—beliefs and actions—or plural balances weighed down by good deeds.
rows.anchor: أي موزونات حسناته من العقائد والأعمال ويجوز أن تكون الموازين جمع ميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful attain every desired thing and escape what they fear.
rows.anchor: الفائزون بكل مطلوب الناجون عن كل مهروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light scales may mean scales of good deeds or deeds carrying no weight—evil deeds—depending on whether unbelievers’ deeds are weighed.
rows.anchor: أي موازين أعماله الحسنة أو أعماله التي لا وزن لها ولا اعتداد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lose themselves waste the time to mature and destroy their capacity to attain perfection.
rows.anchor: ضيعوها بتضييع زمان استكمالها وأبطلو استعدادها لنيل كمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the group by meaning, while singular pronouns follow its grammatical form.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة في الموضعين عبارة عن الموصول وجمعه باعتبار معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Abiding in Hell’ may be a second predicate or explanation; al-Zamakhsharī seems to prefer apposition to the relative clause, which al-Ālūsī rejects with Abū Ḥayyān’s objection that it is strange.
rows.anchor: قال الخفاجي : أي بدل اشتمال لأن خلودهم في جهنم يشتمل على خسرانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioner is God or the tasked angel, not a Hell leader; the question recalls worldly life they wanted back and rebukes denial of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى شأنه أو الملك المأمور بذلك لا بعض رؤساء أهل النار كما قيل

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن كثير
rows.claim: These reciters read qul as an imperative to the angel, not a leader or all condemned represented by one.
rows.anchor: على الأمر للملك لا لبعض الرؤساء كما قيل ولا لجميع الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘How many years did you remain on earth?’ asks how long they lived in the world they seek to return to.
rows.anchor: التي تدعون أن ترجعوا إليها أي كم أقمتم فيها أحياء عدد سنين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: ʿAdadan specifies kam and is temporal adverb for ‘remained’; Abū al-Baqāʾ instead parses it as apposition to kam.
rows.anchor: تمييز لكم وهي ظرف زمان للبثتم وقال : أبو البقاء ( عددا ) بدل من كم

rows.speaker: الأعمش والمفضل عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read ʿadadan with nunation; al-Rāzī takes sinīn as temporal adverb and ʿadadan as a verbal noun used as a noun before its modifier, while Abū al-Baqāʾ makes sinīn appositional.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والمفضل عن عاصم عددا بالتنوين فقال أبو الفضل الرازي سنين نصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their estimate of a day may minimize worldly residence compared with endless Hell; another view says worldly days seemed short because they were days of pleasure.
rows.anchor: استقصارا لمدة لبثهم بالنسبة إلى ما تحققوه من طول زمان خلودهم في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says elapsed time receives little attention, so they assume it was brief.
rows.anchor: لأنها كانت منقضية والمنقضي لا يعتنى بشأنه فلا يدري مقداره طولا وقصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀddīn may be people capable of counting, since torment overwhelms them, or angels counting deeds, as reported from Mujāhid.
rows.anchor: أي المتمكنين من العد فإنا بما دهمنا من العذاب بمعزل من ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن والكسائي
rows.claim: A reading with light dāl means oppressors; followers supposedly called their leaders this for misleading them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والكسائي في رواية ( العادين ) بتخفيف الدال أي الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with doubled yāʾ relates the word to ʿĀd, famed for longevity, and means long-lived ancients who consider the stay brief.
rows.anchor: ( العاديين ) بتشديد الياء جمع عادي نسبة إلى قوم عاد والمراد بهم المعمرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is God or an angel; qul is an imperative to the angel as previously.
rows.anchor: أي الله تعالى أو الملك وقرأ الإخوان ( قل ) على الأمر كما قرآ فيما مر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbs are written without alif in Kufan codices and with alif elsewhere; Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits this, while al-Zamakhsharī reverses it.
rows.anchor: الفعلان في مصاحف الكوفة بغير ألف وبألف في مصاحف مكة والمدينة : والشام والبصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif-less spelling may reflect deletion from the past tense contrary to the rule; Qur’anic orthography has other unusual forms.
rows.anchor: وكأن الرسم بدون ألف يحتمل حذفها من الماضي على خلاف القياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You remained only a little’ confirms their answer; ‘if you knew’ implies they would recognize worldly brevity and avoid earning eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: ما لبثتم

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies ‘you would not have answered with that duration’; this works only if the prior statement refutes rather than confirms their answer.
rows.anchor: وقدر أبو البقاء الجواب لما أجبتم بهذه المدة ولعله يجعل الكلام السابق ردا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively law is optative and needs no consequence; it should not be a connective particle, since that use without wāw is rare or unattested.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ( لو ) للتمني فلا تحتاج لجواب ولا ينبغي أن تجعل وصيلة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Some exegetes ask about graves because they believed the dead became dust and never rose. Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it soundest, but al-Ālūsī objects to the inference from the later clause that they would not return to God.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن عطية أن هذا هو الأصوب وأن قوله سبحانه فيما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report supports asking about worldly residence: after entering Paradise or Hell, people say a day or part of one; the former are praised for mercy, the latter rebuked for fire.
rows.anchor: ما روي مرفوعا أن الله تعالى إذا أدخل أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud sign confirms what precedes; izjāʾ means moving gently and easily; association with insignificant items suggests clouds are negligible before God’s power.
rows.anchor: كالتأكيد لما قبله والتنوير له والإزجاء سوق الشيء برفق وسهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may join one cloud to another; alternatively al-saḥāb is one mass whose parts are joined, supplying the plurality bayna requires.
rows.anchor: بأن يوصل سحابة بسحابة وقال غير واحد : السحاب واحد كالعماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘between the entrance and Ḥawmal’ illustrates bayna with implied plurality; treating clouds as a collective noun is another solution.
rows.anchor: قوله : بين الدخول فحومل واستغنى بعضهم عنه بجعل السحاب اسم جمعي

rows.speaker: ورش عن نافع
rows.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ reads yuʾallifu without hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ورش عن نافع ( يولف ) غير مهموز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukām means clouds piling atop one another; wadq means rain emerging after accumulation.
rows.anchor: أي متراكما بعضه فوق بعض ( فترى الودق

rows.speaker: أبو بحيلة عن أبيه
rows.claim: Abū Buḥayla’s father reportedly glosses wadq as lightning, but al-Ālūsī has not seen this elsewhere; most exegesis and lexicons define it as rain.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي بحيلة عن أبيه أنه فسر الودق بالبرق ولم نره لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kh ilāl are openings formed by accumulation and compression, plural of khall; alternatively singular for a kind, supported by readings from Ibn ʿAbbās and others.
rows.anchor: أي من فتوقه ومخارجه التي حدثت بالتراكم والإنعصار وهو جمع خلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain’s emergence is a circumstantial clause; describing it as seen emerging intensifies speed, like the sea splitting after Moses strikes it.
rows.anchor: لأن الرؤية بصرية وفي تعقيب الجعل المذكور برؤيته خارجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From the sky’ may mean clouds, since anything above is sky, or the upper direction; naming the sky suggests height’s role in precipitation.
rows.anchor: فإن كل ما علاك سماء وكأنه العدول عنه إلى السماء للإيماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Mountains’ may mean huge cloud masses; the claim that they are things God created from hail is linguistically unsupported.
rows.anchor: قطع عظام تشبه الجبال في العظم على التشبيه البليغ

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī says mountains are things God created from hail, a reading rejected as unsupported by language.
rows.anchor: قول الأصبهاني : إن الجبال ما جبله الله تعالى أي خلقه

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī takes the second min as partitive like the third and also as apposition; al-Ālūsī calls this a clear error.
rows.anchor: وزعم الحوفي أن من الثانية للتبعيض كالثالثة مع قوله بالبدلية وهو خطأ ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes the first min origin, second partitive in object position, and third explanatory: some mountains or hail mountains in the sky descend, namely hail.
rows.anchor: من الأولى ابتدائية والثانية للتبعيض واقعة موقع المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hail strikes whom God wills, harming property and person, while He diverts it from others; the pronouns most naturally refer to hail.
rows.anchor: أي يصيبه فيناله ما يناله من ضرر في ماله ونفسه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the second and third min as additional, with the first phrase object and second appositional, yielding hail from the sky.
rows.anchor: إن ( من ) الثانية ومن الثالثة زائدتان وكل من المجرورين في محل نصب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ considers both particles additional; the first phrase is object, while the second may say hail rather than stones is in the mountains, with its pronoun referring to mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : هما زائدتان إلا أن المجرور بأولاهما في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil’s poetry about mountains of poetry illustrates mountain as metaphor for abundance; expressions also speak of mountains of gold or knowledge.
rows.anchor: قول ابن مقبل : إذا مت عن ذكر القوافي فلن ترى لها شاعرا مني أطلب

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Mujāhid, al-Kalbī, and most exegetes take sky and mountains literally: God created mountains of hail in the sky as stone mountains on earth, and reason has no decisive objection.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد والكلبي وأكثر المفسرين أن المراد بالسماء المظلمة وبالجبال حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A natural-philosophical account traces rain, snow, hail, and frost to celestial forces, vapor, cooling, and condensation, with wind and heat shaping the outcomes.
rows.anchor: والمشهور بين أهل الحكمة أن انبعاث قوى السماويات وأشعتها قد يوجب تصعيد أجسام لطيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All such processes depend on God’s will and wisdom; natural causes are customary and celestial first causes make ‘from the sky’ apt. This account preserves eloquence and avoids popular doubts.
rows.anchor: والحق أن كل ذلك مستند إلى إرادة الله عز وجل ومشيئته سبحانه المبنية على الحكم والمصالح

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr suggests the pronouns could refer to rain, which more commonly benefits and is directed or withheld; al-Ālūsī considers this remote and objectionable.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر يحتمل رجوعهما إلى ( الودق ) والبرد فيهما مجرى اسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning belongs to the cloud above; its possessive precedes explicit mention because existence is obvious, and referring it to hail is rejected.
rows.anchor: أي ضوء برق السحاب الموصوف بما مر من الإزجاء والتأليف

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa reads sanāʾ long and barq with bāʾ and rāʾ open as plural barqah; another variant follows the bāʾ’s vowel, while sanāʾ denotes elevation and intense light.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف ( سناء ) ممدودا ( برقه ) بضم الباء وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading assimilates dāl into sīn in yakādu sanā; lightning nearly overwhelms sight by sudden intensity, and ‘eyes’ heightens the threat.
rows.anchor: أي يحفظها من فرط الإضاءة وسرعة ورودها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yudhhibu with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on hāʾ; critics fault its transitivity markers, but al-Ālūsī defends the transmitted reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ( يذهب ) بضم الياء وكسر الهاء وذهب الأخفش وأبو حاتم إلى تخطئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading may add bāʾ, making ‘eyes’ the object, or use bāʾ meaning ‘from’ with ‘light’ understood; al-Ḥarīrī allows both transitivity markers.
rows.anchor: على زيادة الباء أي يذهب الأبصار وعلى أن الباء بمعنى من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning producing the opposite of its dark cloud is a strong sign of God’s complete power.
rows.anchor: من أقوى الدلائل على كمال القدرة من حيث أنه توليد للضد من الضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilfah may mean night and day alternate, each replacing the other in appropriate activities; this is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: بأن يقوم مقامه فيما ينبغي أي يعمل فيه وروي هذا عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, one succeeds and follows the other; khilfah names the resulting state.
rows.anchor: بأن يعقبه ويجيء بعده وهو اسم للحالة من خلف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Some read khilfah as difference in length or darkness and brightness, the latter attributed to Mujāhid; it may encompass both and other contrasts.
rows.anchor: والمراد الاختلاف في الزيادة والنقصان كما قيل أو في السواد والبياض كما روي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: البحر وزهير
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr cites an idiom for frequent trips to relieve oneself; Zuhayr’s verse about animals following behind illustrates repeated succession.
rows.anchor: بفلان خلفة واختلاف إذا اختلف كثيرا إلى متبرزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poet depicts a woman moving between winter and summer homes, illustrating repeated alternation.
rows.anchor: يصف امرأة تنتقل من منزل في الشتاء إلى منزل في الصيف دأبا

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines khalf and khilfah as mutually different; this needs no omitted ‘possessing alternation,’ since singular names the difference.
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس الخلف والخلفة بالكسر المختلف وعليه لاحاجة إلى تقدير المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that each of night and day frequently comes and goes.
rows.anchor: المراد يذهب كل منهما ويجيء كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternation lets one make up a devotional portion missed in one period during the other; early authorities transmit this sense.
rows.anchor: ليكونا وقتين للمتذكر من فاته ورده من العبادة في أحدهما تداركه في الآخر

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Al-Ṭayālisī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim report that ʿUmar prolonged forenoon prayer to complete a missed litany and recited the verse.
rows.anchor: وروى الطيالسي وابن أبي حاتم أن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه أطال صلاة الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering may figuratively mean making up missed worship; Majmaʿ al-Bayān also says voluntary prayer after obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: وكأن التذكر مجاز عن اداء ما فات وهو مما يتوقف الاداء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another good reading is reflection on God’s creative signs and gratitude for blessings in night and day; the author says it nearly eclipses alternatives absent transmitted views.
rows.anchor: أن يتذكر ويتفكر في بدائع صنع الله تعالى فيعلم أنه لابد لما ذكر من صانع حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may attach to ‘made’ or express purpose; aw distributes the senses or permits either independently, while the longer wording emphasizes remembrance.
rows.anchor: أن اللام على هذا صلة ( جعل ) ولما كان ظهور فائدة ذلك

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy reads an yatadhakkara, the original form before tāʾ changes to dhāl and assimilates.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب ( أن يتذكر ) وهو أصل ليذكر فابدل التاء ذالا وأدغم

rows.speaker: النخعي وابن وثاب وزيد بن علي وطلحة وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers use yadhkura, the form-II imperfect meaning ‘remember.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ النخعي وابن وثاب وزيد بن علي وطلحة وحمزة ( أن يذكر ) مضارع ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This resumes the earlier mention of winds: they stir and spread clouds, then spread them as one mass or make pieces, according to God’s will.
rows.anchor: مسوق لبيان ما أجمل فيما سبق من أحوال الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In the sky’ means in its direction, not inside the sky in the ordinary sense; clouds may travel, stop, and cover all or part.
rows.anchor: في سمتها لا في نفس السماء بالمعنى المتبادر

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads kusfan with still sīn; it may be shortened, plural of kusfah, verbal noun, or description with an omitted ‘possessing pieces.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن عامر بسكون السين على أنه مخفف من المفتوح أو جمع كسفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wadq is rain emerging through cloud openings in connected and fragmented states; the pronoun refers to the masculine collective noun ‘cloud.’
rows.anchor: أي المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the still-sīn reading, the pronoun might refer to kasf itself, but al-Ālūsī calls this unsound.
rows.anchor: على قراءة ( كسفا ) بالسكون أن يكون له وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain reaching lands of whichever servants God wills brings sudden joy at fertile abundance; the bāʾ is transitive.
rows.anchor: والباء في ( به ) للتعدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is a subject and predicate: God began people weak, with weakness metaphorically their foundation; min marks origin.
rows.anchor: ابتدأكم ضعفاء وجعل الضعف أساس أمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, weakness means ‘the weak’ as emphatic verbal noun, ‘one with weakness,’ or sperm as weak origin, a view attributed to Qatāda; initial weakness better fits the next stage.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفسير وإن كان مأثورا عن قتادة إلا أن الأول أولى وأنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strength follows childhood weakness at puberty or when spirit attaches to bodies; weakness and gray hair follow strength with age.
rows.anchor: وذلك عند بلوغكم الحلم

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة وعبد الله وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, with readings from ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Rajāʾ, open the ḍād; most use ḍamma. Both are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: وفتح عاصم وحمزة ضاد ( ضعف ) في الجمع

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet corrected fatḥa to ḍamma as his people’s dialect; this did not reject the other transmitted reading.
rows.anchor: لغة قومه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: عاصم وأبو عبد الرحمن والجحدري والضحاك
rows.claim: Other transmissions from ʿĀṣim use ḍamma throughout or first two forms and fatḥa last; others use ḍamma first and fatḥa later.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا الضم في الأولين والفتح في الأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish bodily weakness with ḍamma from intellectual weakness with fatḥa; al-Ālūsī sees no difference and says either may describe both.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لا فرق بين المضموم والمفتوح وكونهما مما يوصف به البدن والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second weakness refers to the first, while the last is old-age weakness; repetition is indefinite to match strength, despite strained attempts to distinguish repetitions.
rows.anchor: والمراد بضعف الثاني عين الأول ونكر لمشاكلة ( قوة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates these stages by creating causes and locations or the states themselves; the direct reading needs no figurative reinterpretation.
rows.anchor: وخلقها إما بمعنى خلق أسبابها أو محالها وأما إيجادها أنفسها وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing stages plainly demonstrate God’s knowledge and power despite possible alternative life courses.
rows.anchor: من أوضح دلائل العلم والقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sāʿah means Resurrection, named as the final worldly hour or because it arrives suddenly; ‘rising’ means its existence or creatures standing in it.
rows.anchor: سميت بها لأنها تقوم في آخر ساعة من ساعات الدنيا أو لأنها تقع بغتة

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say criminals swear they stayed only an hour in graves after death; al-Ālūsī prefers this because the stay continues until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: كما روى عن الكلبي ومقاتل والمراد به ما أقاموا بعد الموت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda instead says they mean they spent no more than an hour in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وروى غير واحد عن قتادة أنهم يعنون ما لبثوا في الدنيا غير ساعة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Another view concerns the interval before resurrection. Abū Hurayra’s report says it is forty but omits the unit; al-Ālūsī says only God knows and rejects claimed consensus for forty years.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ما بين النفختين أربعون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the claim occurs when punishment is interrupted and they lie to minimize their stay, or forget it in terror; they may compare with coming punishment.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري أن ذلك وقت ينقطع عذابهم فيه وأستقلوا مدة لبثهم كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may call life an hour because they gained nothing: much without benefit is little, while little with benefit is much, expressing regret for wasted life.
rows.anchor: لعدم إنتفاعهم بها والكثير بلا نفع قليل كما أن القليل مع النفع كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses complete paronomasia between Resurrection and an hour of time; inflection and the article do not spoil it because the first became a proper name.
rows.anchor: وبين الساعة وساعة جناس تام مماثل كما أطبق عليه البلغاء

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Ḥajar proposes a second Quranic pun treating the second ‘eyes’ as insight; al-Ālūsī rejects it as metaphor and irregular plural of baṣīrah.
rows.anchor: وأستنبط شيخ الإسلام إبن حجر عليه الرحمة موضعا آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describes persistent denial or their astonishing delusion about life’s length now that it was an hour, to spur them from worldly attachment; God, Satan, or desire may be the agent, but their choices remain responsible, and one view says unbelievers can lie after death.
rows.anchor: في وصف المجرمين بالتمادي في التكذيب والإصرار على الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some use this verse to deny punishment in the grave, but al-Ālūsī says that inference is unsound.
rows.anchor: وأستدل بها بعضهم على نفي عذاب القبر وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn is an iftiʿāl form of ṣarākh, intense shouting, with original tāʾ changed to ṭāʾ; it often means calling for rescue.
rows.anchor: إفتعال من الصراخ وهو شدة الصياح والأصل يصترخون فأبدلت التاء طاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they seek rescue from God; the suggestion they call to one another in bewilderment is rejected.
rows.anchor: وبه فسره هنا قتادة فقال : يستغيثون فيها واستغاثتهم بالله عزوجل بدليل ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea may be introduced by implied ‘saying’ and coordinated with prior speech, stand independently as an explanation, or function as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: بإضمار القول أي ويقولون بالعطف أو يقولون بدونه على أنه تفسير لما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling requested work different from former work expresses regret and desire to repair admitted wrongdoing; alternatively, they mistakenly thought past conduct good.
rows.anchor: وتقييد العمل الصالح بالوصف المذكور للتحسر على ما عملوه من غير الصالح

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ offers parses making ṣāliḥan and ghayra modifiers of omitted nouns, or ṣāliḥan a modifier and ghayra the object of ‘we do.’
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكونا صفتين لمصدر محذوف أو لمفعول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to leave Hell and return to worldly life for righteous work, especially affirming God’s unity, obeying the Messenger, and submitting.
rows.anchor: فالمراد أخرجنا من النار وردنا إلى الدنيا نعمل صالحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ‘we do righteous work’ as saying lā ilāha illā Allāh.
rows.anchor: نعمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine question rebukes their plea and denies God failed to give ample time for reflection and reminders.
rows.anchor: جواب من جهته تعالى وتوبيخ لهم في الآخرة حين يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā means the age or span of years in which anyone wishing to remember could reflect and be reminded.
rows.anchor: أي العمر الذي أو عمرا يتذكر فيه من تذكر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes mā as a temporal verbal noun; this is challenged because fīhi cannot refer to it unless treated as a noun or refers to age implied by ‘We gave you long life.’
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : ما مصدرية ظرفية أي ألم نعمركم في مدة تذكر

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says making mā negative is untenable in wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: وجعل ما نافية لا يصح كما قال إبن الحاجب لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī, authenticated by al-Ḥākim from Ibn ʿAbbās, sets sufficient lifetime at sixty; Sahl ibn Saʿd reports God keeps a person alive to sixty to remove excuses.
rows.anchor: على ما روى عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وأخرجه جماعة وصححه الحاكم عن إبن عباس ستون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other estimates are fifty, forty-six (Ibn ʿAbbās), forty or puberty (al-Ḥasan), seventeen, eighteen (Qatāda), twenty (ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz), and twenty to sixty (Mujāhid).
rows.anchor: خمسون سنة وفي رواية عن إبن عباس أنه ست وأربعون سنة

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads mā yadhkur fīhi man udhkira with assimilation and pronounces the connecting hamzat al-waṣl in connected speech.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ( ما يذكر فيه من أذكر ) بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The warner came to you’ coordinates with the question’s meaning, effectively ‘We gave you life and the warner came’; another parse coordinates it with ‘We gave you life.’
rows.anchor: فكأنه قيل : عمرناكم وجاءكم النذير

rows.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd identify the warner as Muḥammad; another view says the Qur’an, while Abū Ḥayyān takes all prophets, supported by the plural al-nudhur.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنذير على ما روى عن السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة ووكيع والحسين بن الفضل والفراء والطبري
rows.claim: These authorities say the warner is gray hair; a report makes each white hair warn its neighbor of death, and poetry likewise calls gray hair a herald.
rows.anchor: وعن إبن عباس وعكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة ووكيع والحسين بن الفضل والفراء والطبري هو الشيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other warners are fever, deaths of relatives, or maturity of reason; the singular ‘warner’ fits the immediate point.
rows.anchor: موت الأهل والأقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to taste punishment follows from long life and the warner’s arrival; denial of a helper is causal, ‘wrongdoers’ means unbelievers, and naming them rebukes them.
rows.anchor: لترتيب الأمر بالذوق على ما قبلها من التعمير ومجيء النذير
